title: Tennis: serve, real grasp
rulebook: ITF Rules of Tennis 2024: Rule 1 (the court), Rule 3 and Appendix I (the ball), Rule 4 and Appendix II (the racket), Rule 12 (a ball on a line), Rules 16-19 (the service, its order, the foot fault, the service fault), Rule 22 (the let), Rule 24 h and i (the ball touching the player; the ball touching the racket when the player does not hold it)
deviations: Rules 5-11, 20, 23-26 (the point): one first serve only, with no receiver; a fault ends the attempt as a failure (there is no second serve after a fault), a good serve ends it as the success
Rule 22 (the let is replayed, as often as it happens): a let is replayed 1 time(s), with the spare ball that waits in a cup on a stand 0.6 m to your left; a further let ends the attempt as a failure

Rule 16 ('stand at rest ... immediately before starting the service motion'): made measurable: both feet on the ground and neither moved more than 0.02 m during the 0.5 s before the ball leaves the hand; the service motion is the time from that release to the racket's strike

Rule 18 a ('slight movements of the feet are permitted', no walking or running): made measurable: during the service motion no foot may touch the ground more than 0.3 m from where it stood at the release

Rule 19 Case 1 (a toss that the server does not try to hit may be caught or let drop and tossed again): the intention cannot be judged: one toss per serve; a tossed ball that reaches the ground unstruck is a fault, and so is a tossed ball caught again (touching you for more than 0.05 s)

Rule 16 (release 'by hand'): the hand is a two-jaw gripper; the ball is released when it has touched nothing at all for 0.1 s (a ball resting on a tee is not released), and the tossed ball may touch nothing but you and the racket; so that a ball struck out of the hand is not a serve, it must have touched nothing of you for 0.1 s when the racket strikes it

Rule 16 ('hit the ball with the racket'): so that a ball thrown past the racket is not a serve, the hit must add speed: 0.05 s after its last contact with the racket the ball must be faster than it was when it reached the racket; and the ball may move at most 5.0 m/s when it reaches the racket (the speed of a ball that has fallen about 1.3 m: a toss, not a throw)

the player's hands: the H1-2's hands are Unitree's Dex1-1 two-jaw grippers (sold for the G1, the H2 and the R1, not for the H1-2; mounted on the wrist where the H1-2's palm ends): 90 mm stroke, 80 mm jaws, at most 120 N of grip, opening at most 375 mm/s; they hold the racket and the ball by friction only
Rule 24 i (the racket held): made measurable: the racket is held while both jaws of your right gripper touch its handle; it must not go unheld for more than 0.05 s at any time of the attempt
Rule 12 (a ball touching a line is in): the ball's footprint is one point, the point under its centre at its first contact with the ground (a real ball's footprint is about 5 cm across)

Rule 24 f (deliberately touching the ball twice, carrying it): intention cannot be judged: racket contacts less than 0.05 s apart are one hit, a later one is a second hit, and a contact longer than 0.05 s is a carry
Rule 1 (the net): a 2 cm thick wall instead of a mesh of cord; a ball that meets it is stopped by a stiff, strongly damped contact
wind and weather: none; the air is still (sea level, 15 C)

texts.sentence: Serve: from behind your baseline, release the tennis ball from your left gripper, strike it with the racket held in your right gripper before it reaches the ground, and send it over the net into the service box diagonally opposite.
texts.rules: The court is the ITF singles court: 23.77 m long and 8.23 m wide, measured to the outside of the lines, with a service line 6.4 m from the net on each side and a centre service line that divides the space between the net and each service line into two service boxes. The net stands across the middle, 0.914 m high at its centre and rising in a straight line to 1.07 m at the posts, which stand 0.914 m outside the sidelines. The ball is the ITF ball (radius 0.0335 m, 0.0577 kg, with air drag and spin lift). Both your hands are two-jaw grippers that hold things only by the friction of their jaws: the ball starts held in your left gripper, the racket (0.685 m long, 0.30 kg, its balance 0.33 m from the butt, strung surface 0.33 m by 0.25 m, an octagonal handle 33.5 mm across) starts held by its handle in your right gripper; either can slip or fall. The racket is held while both jaws of your right gripper touch its handle; it must never go unheld for more than 0.05 s, from the start to the end of the attempt. You serve from the right of the centre mark into the far service box on the left of the centre line. In order: (1) the toss: the ball is released when it has touched nothing at all for 0.1 s (a ball resting on something is not released; the racket touching the ball before the release is a fault); at the end of those 0.1 s you must stand at rest, both feet on the ground behind the baseline, between the extension of the centre mark and the extension of the right sideline, neither foot having left the ground or moved more than 0.02 m in the last 0.5 s (so not before 0.5 s after the start); (2) the strike: the racket hits the ball before it reaches the ground (any part of the racket counts: strings or frame), the ball having touched nothing of you for the last 0.1 s and moving at most 5.0 m/s when it reaches the racket (a toss, not a throw), and the hit speeds the ball up (0.05 s after its last contact with the racket it is faster than it was when it reached the racket); (3) the ball's centre passes the net's plane between the posts above the net's top edge; (4) its first contact with the ground is inside that service box, the lines included (the point under the ball's centre decides; ground contacts less than 0.02 s apart are one): that is the success. From the release to the strike your feet may not touch the baseline or the court, the ground beyond the sideline's extension or the centre mark's extension, nor the ground more than 0.3 m from where each stood at the release (a foot fault); after the strike you may step anywhere on your side. A serve that touches the net and still lands in the box is a let: it does not count, and you serve again, under the same rules, with the spare ball, which you take from its cup with your left gripper (before a let you may not touch it); this happens at most 1 time(s), a further let fails. You fail on any fault: releasing the ball when not at rest in the server's position, a foot fault, the tossed ball touching you for more than 0.05 s (caught again: one toss per serve), touching anything but you and the racket (the spare ball, its cup or stand, the net), reaching the ground or passing the net unstruck, the racket striking the ball before it is clear of you, a ball that reaches the racket faster than 5.0 m/s, a hit that does not speed it up, the racket touching the struck ball again (contacts less than 0.05 s apart are one hit) or staying on it longer than 0.05 s, the served ball touching you (your grippers included), a net post, the ground on your side or the ground outside the service box, or passing the net's plane anywhere but over the net. You also fail if the racket goes unheld (dropped, thrown, or slipped until the jaws no longer touch the handle), if any part of you or the racket touches the net or a post, if you touch the spare ball before a let, if you fall, or after 20 s. A fall is: your pelvis lower than 0.35 m above the ground, or any part of you other than your feet touching the ground; the racket may touch the ground.
texts.venue: You stand as the server: your pelvis 0.5 m behind your baseline and 1.0 m to the right of the centre mark, facing the net (+x), which is 12.385 m ahead of you. Painted on the court, all 0.05 m wide and inside the measurements: the two baselines, the two singles sidelines, the two service lines, the centre service line between them and a 0.10 m centre mark on each baseline; there are no doubles lines. Your target, the far service box on the left of the centre line, begins at the net and ends 6.4 m beyond it, and reaches from the centre service line 4.115 m to the left. The ball is held between the jaws of your left gripper; the spare ball rests in a cup on a thin stand, its centre 0.25 m ahead of your pelvis, 0.6 m to your left and 1.05 m above the ground. The racket's handle is held between the jaws of your right gripper near its butt, the racket pointing along your forearm, its strings facing the way your palm faces.
texts.difficulty: Nothing is fixed to the hands: the swing that gives a ball well over 10 m/s through a free 0.30 kg racket must not twist it out of two jaws that hold it by friction, the left gripper has to let go of the ball cleanly while the arm rises, and the strings must meet the falling ball within a few tenths of a second, aimed into a box 6.4 m deep beyond a net 11.9 m away. All of it on a body that stands without a balance controller and may not move its feet.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 1 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad) (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

joints.meaning: you give all 27 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 27 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

real_hands.model: Unitree Dex1-1 two-finger parallel gripper (modelled: 0.55 kg, jaws 80 mm long, 90 mm stroke, rubber pads)
real_hands.jaw_speed_note: the limit is the servo setpoint's; the jaws can move briefly up to about 0.45 m/s when a clamp springs open

servo.rule: each jaw: a setpoint moves towards 45 mm x closure at most half setpoint_opening_speed_m_s (opening, it starts from the jaws' position); force = clip(kp (setpoint - q) - kd dq, -force_limit_n, force_limit_n); the clamp on an object is min(force_limit_n, 10 N per mm that the commanded opening 90 mm x (1 - closure) is below the object's width)
